raw_response:
I am 72 years old and have farmed these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 55 years. I finished high school, so I read fertilizer labels, keep my own cost books, and calculate input-output in my head. I do not need an outsider to tell me what my soil needs—I know every ridge and low spot. I split my land into two blocks: 5 mu stays in the wheat-maize double crop because that is my food security and stable base; 5.1 mu goes to hybrid chili because Quzhou prices have been decent for dried chili and I have the well water to support the extra irrigation.

My wheat went in last October after deep ploughing. I used an improved hard-grain wheat variety. Now it is greening up, so in mid-March I will topdress 25 kg of urea per mu when the soil warms. Last fall I already put down 50 kg per mu of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer as basal, so my total nutrient budget for this wheat crop is about 19 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times from March to May—green-up water, jointing water, and heading water. My well has never run dry in spring. I spray fungicide twice for rust and powdery mildew, and one insecticide spray if aphids show up. I got 560 kg per mu last year; I expect 550 this year.

Right after wheat harvest in early June, I immediately rotary-till that same 5 mu and plant hybrid maize. I use Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whichever the dealer in town has in stock and my neighbors had good luck with. At planting I band 50 kg per mu of 20-10-10 compound fertilizer, and at the big-flare stage I side-dress 25 kg per mu of urea. That works out to roughly 20 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: once right after planting if June turns hot and dry, once at jointing, and once at tasseling. I use acetochlor for weeds and spray for corn borer if I see moth eggs. I target 650 kg per mu.

For the 5.1 mu of chili, I start field prep in April. I deep-plough and ridge the soil because chili roots need loose soil down to 25 cm. I plant a hybrid variety I switched to three years ago after my neighbor got over 2,000 kg per mu fresh with it. My basal dressing is 1,000 kg per mu of rotted chicken manure plus 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer. Then at first flowering and again at heavy fruiting, I side-dress 15 kg per mu of urea and 20 kg per mu of potassium sulfate. That totals about 22 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 18 kg potassium per mu. Chili is a potassium hog—I figured that out from my own notebooks and from watching plants drop flowers when K is low. I irrigate seven times through the season, keeping the ridges moist but never waterlogged. I spray five times: aphids, thrips, mites, anthracnose, and a viral-disease prevention. I hire three local women for transplanting and picking because at my age I cannot bend all day anymore. I expect 2,200 kg per mu of fresh chili.

I watch my neighbors every morning. If Old Wang adds 5 kg more urea to his wheat this spring, I do the same—it costs me maybe 15 yuan per mu extra, but a yield drop would cost me 200 yuan. Fertilizer prices are high again this year, but a bad harvest is a disaster while wasting a little fertilizer is only a cost. My grandson checks prices on his phone, and I compare with the dealer in town. I keep a notebook: every jin of seed, every bag of fertilizer, every irrigation hour. After 55 years I trust my own records more than anyone else’s mouth.
